correctness.rationale: The exponential-time representation of R gives entrywise nonnegativity, and M=(R−(1−θ)I)/θ reduces the positivity test to its diagonal for θ>0. Discounted occupation before departure and after the first return gives R_ii(s)=[1+r_i E{s(1−exp(−T_i/s))}]⁻¹, retaining T_i=∞ rather than conditioning on return. The integrand increases strictly to T_i for both finite positive times and ∞, and is bounded by s near zero. Monotone convergence therefore gives the specified limit, including zero for a transient state; renewal reward gives the stationary mass in each closed class. Absorbing diagonals are constant one. This proves the exact crossing criterion with equality included; θ=0 is the Euler diagonal test and θ=1 is a nonnegative resolvent. Reversal preserves the diagonal and the Euler exit rates. The recorded rational tests are finite corroboration only; the frozen script was inspected, not executed.

evidence: For N≥2 add ε times an all-to-all conservative generator. The perturbed resolvent diagonals are strictly decreasing by the earlier theorem and converge for every fixed s to the original ones by matrix inversion continuity. The limiting diagonals are nonincreasing. An equality at two distinct s would force a plateau, hence constancy by analyticity, impossible when R′_ii(0)=−r_i<0. An absorbing row is constant one. The large-s limit is the Abel mean of p_ii(t), which tends to zero for transient states and to the within-class stationary mass for closed recurrent states.
